fact: Madagascar's Ministry of Technical Education and Vocational Training signed a partnership with Orange Madagascar on 8 October 2026 to develop digital-skills training frameworks and learning pathways for young people and women.

Madagascar's Ministry of Technical Education and Vocational Training signed a partnership with GIP Pix on 11 September 2026 to prepare young people for, and certify, digital skills, across eight axes including exam centres and trainer training.

Madagascar's Ministry of Technical Education and Vocational Training and the OIF launched on 19 January 2026 a new phase of D-CLIC to train 1,000 young people free in digital skills by mid-2026, within a goal of 40,000 by 2028.
The Ministry of Technical Education and Vocational Training adopted a UNESCO-backed digitalisation strategy targeting 40,000 people trained in digital skills by 2028, 6,000 a year.
